chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: As I read it, this definition seems to assume that ECN marking corresponds to overload, while the ECN documents seem to expect that the indiciation is that we are getting closer than we want to overload.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: (That was in reference to the draft definition of "Overload".)

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: The overload alleviation in this draft is not dependent on ECN marking, it is based on local detection of link utilization

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: My concern isn't dependence.  It is that as written the draft defines that the conditions which cause ECN marking are a form of overload.  That is not how the ECN folks have talked about their work.  I think we need to be more nuanced in our terminology.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: Got your point, the overload definition here is not related to ECN marking, maybe it can be clariifed later

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: What decision does the summary table help an operator make? Are all the options viable, with none better than the others?

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: Pavan imo it's to emphasise a given solution:  "it depends"

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: Thanks Andrew, understood on "it depends". My point is that the current framing isn't helping as much as it could. Section 3 lists the common functional actions (e.g., measurement, trigger, notification, steering) but doesn't map them onto the approaches in Section 4. A table with those actions as rows and the approaches as columns would show how much they overlap and where each one really differs, which would make "it depends" easier to act on.

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: true, a clear table how each solution approaches the function would make comparison easier
